newsitem.title: USA: Allegheny seeks to compete in Pittsburgh.
newsitem.headline: Allegheny seeks to compete in Pittsburgh.

text.p: Allegheny Power System Inc said it asked the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission to allow electric utility competition in two "retail energy zones" in Pittsburgh.
The company said its petition supports a request made last week by the City of Pittsburgh to establish competition in the zones, which are vacant sites slated for development.
In announcing its filing, the city said commission approval will allow customers to choose between current established rates for Allegheny's West Penn subsidiary and DQE Inc's Duquesne Light.

The city said its filing was made in anticipation of West Penn's effort to expand its service teritory to include the areas, which it described as the two major development tracts in the city. The areas, known as the Nine Mile Run and South Side Works site, cover a total of more than 350 acres.
Allegheny Power says West Penn's electric rates, which are the lowest in Pennsylvania, will help to attract development to the sites. The entire city is now served by Duquesne Light.
The city said site preparation is slated to begin next spring on the sites where a mix of residential, commercial and industrial development is expected to be located.
